messages:
maria: quick sync — sketching a lean operator API for dedicated GPU pools: two primitives: reserve(request) and release(id). keeps reconciliation minimal.
kevin: short + sweet. how do we support fast spikes? tenants want short-lived headroom.
maria: ephemeral reservations with ttl. they behave like normal reservations but are low-priority and auto-expire. operator reclaims capacity and emits usage events.
olivia: sounds fine but we must tie to billing. ephemeral should prepay an allocation_fee that is amortized on release. prevents surprise cold-start costs.
zane: client crash handling? we need leak detection and partial refunds for ephemerals. operator should run a GC loop that reconciles expired reservations and posts a settlement event.
dan: reuse the existing token ledger for final settlement. operator emits {reservation_id, tenant, allocated_fee, used_units} as an event; ledger consumes and updates balances. avoids duplicated accounting logic.
kevin: what about admission when capacity is tight? queue vs fallback?
maria: return structured failures: {code: "NO_CAPACITY", retry_after: 30s, fallback: "smaller_model|quantized_variant", queue_pos: 12}. client decides. operator can optionally offer recommended fallback_model.
olivia: we should also enforce tenant soft-caps and concurrent-reservation limits so one noisy tenant doesn't hog ephemeral pool. admission must be atomic across quota checks and allocation.
zane: +1. also require idempotency_key on reserve calls so retries are safe. store key and return existing reservation if duplicate.
dan: metrics: reservation_latency_ms, allocations_per_tenant, refunds/sec, expired_ephemeral_count. add a dedicated dashboard and alert on refund spikes.
maria: warmup billing nuance: if GPU spin-up takes N seconds, allocate an upfront warmup_fee that's pro-rated and then reconciled on release. document the formula in the RFC.
kevin: autoscaling behavior: operator should prefer vertical packing (reuse existing nodes) and only scale out if tail latency projections exceed SLOs. use moving-window demand and recent ephemeral churn to predict short spikes.
olivia: predicted scaling must be conservative to avoid oscillation. add a hysteresis window and min-stable-duration for new nodes.
zane: also expose a "prewarm_hint" from the reserve API so callers can indicate expected session length or model. operator can use that for better packing.
dan: failure modes section: network partition, double-reserve, ledger timeout. define compensating actions: mark reservation as pending-settlement and prevent double-charge.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: orch-reserve-release-v2 -> staging at 23:00 UTC :rocket:
maria: next steps: i'll draft a short RFC with API shapes, event schemas (flat fields only), and failure handling. will include example billing flows and dashboard mockups.
kevin: add a short compatibility note for dedicated vs hosted: hosted may map ephemeral to a lower-cost variant automatically.
olivia: will champion observability PR. add logs for idempotency_key hits and GC evictions.
zane: i'll prototype the idempotency store and GC sweeper.
dan: i can wire the ledger consumer for settlement events.
maria: great — RFC by EOD tomorrow. feedback welcome. :thumbsup:
